solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: They help you to discern good young women (7)

blocks.note: G = good
lasses are girls or young women

annotation.surface: Someone with an eye for good young women, and what helps them see.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Discern' looks like judging character, but it just means see clearly, which is what spectacles help you do.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: spectacles help the wearer see things clearly.

entries.clue: Gourmet primarily fed on gold dessert (6)

indicatorNotes.primarily: primarily means first of all, so only the first letter of 'Gourmet' is used

blocks.note: first letter of Gourmet
to have fed is to have eaten: ATE
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

annotation.surface: A gourmet who dined on a dessert covered in gold leaf.
annotation.walkthrough: AU for gold comes from the Latin aurum and turns up in crosswords constantly.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain hypernym: a gateau is a rich layered cake served as a dessert.

entries.clue: Discriminatory article on spirit (6)

blocks.note: 'a' is the indefinite article
Geist is German for spirit, as in poltergeist and zeitgeist

annotation.surface: A newspaper piece on the spirit of the age, accused of bias.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means sitting on top, so A goes above GEIST.
annotation.definitionFit: An ageist attitude discriminates against people because of their age.

entries.clue: Very advanced religious leader guns for popular entertainment (4,5)

blocks.note: 'so' = very, as in so good
A = advanced, as in A level
the Pope leads the Catholic Church
RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners

annotation.surface: An aged cleric trades his weapons for a night of TV.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Very advanced' reads as 'very old', but the two words are separate pieces, SO and A.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain hypernym: a soap opera is a long-running TV or radio drama with a mass audience.

entries.clue: Second writer redrafted third paper for waster (11)

indicatorNotes.redrafted: a redrafted text is rewritten in a new form, so the letters of THIRD are rearranged

blocks.note: S = second
a pen is the thing that writes
THIRD rearranged
the FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

annotation.surface: A second-string journalist rewrites the third piece for a feckless subject.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Writer' is the pen, not the person, a common crossword trick.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who squanders money freely is called a waster.

entries.clue: A muppet turned on hotel boiler replacement? (4,4)

indicatorNotes.turned: to turn something is to change its shape or order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters
H = hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: Some fool switched on the hotel's new heating system.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: a heat pump is one modern alternative to a gas boiler.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: heat pumps are being installed in place of gas boilers to heat homes.

entries.clue: Overpromote extremes of healthy exercise (4)

indicatorNotes.extremes of: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so H and Y from 'healthy'

blocks.note: first and last letters of healthy
PE is physical education, school exercise

annotation.surface: A warning against overselling the benefits of a workout.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a complaint about fitness marketing, which is itself the kind of overselling the definition describes.
annotation.definitionFit: To hype something is to promote it far beyond its merits.

entries.clue: A typical cop’s corruption is disastrous (11)

indicatorNotes.corruption: a corrupted text is garbled, so the letters of 'a typical cop' are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

annotation.surface: A cynical verdict that police corruption has ruinous effects.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Corruption' does double duty in the surface, as the bent copper and as the instruction to scramble.
annotation.definitionFit: Apocalyptic means foretelling or amounting to utter catastrophe, so disastrous.

entries.clue: Algeciras? Capital! (4,2,5)

blocks.note: Algeciras is a Spanish harbour town near Gibraltar; the question mark says it is one example
a Caribbean capital city whose name describes the first half

annotation.walkthrough: The first half is a description, a port of Spain, and the second is the proper name of a Caribbean capital; the punctuation marks the example and the reveal.
annotation.definitionFit: Algeciras is one Spanish port, and Port of Spain is the capital city of Trinidad and Tobago.

entries.clue: Expert worries mounting in rugby contest (9)

indicatorNotes.mounting: in a down clue, mounting means climbing upwards, so FRETS is read bottom to top
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' puts the turned word inside MAUL

blocks.note: to fret is to worry
a maul is a rugby scrum-like tussle for a ball carried in hand

annotation.surface: Anxiety building up in the middle of a rugby match.
annotation.walkthrough: In rugby a maul forms when players bind around the ball carrier and push; the reversed FRETS sits in its middle.
annotation.definitionFit: Masterful can mean showing great skill, so expert.

entries.clue: Unhealthy-looking pig gobbles the lot (6)

indicatorNotes.gobbles: what a pig gobbles goes inside it, so ALL goes inside SOW

blocks.note: a sow is a female pig
the lot = everything, all

annotation.surface: A greedy, pasty-faced pig eats everything in the trough.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unhealthy-looking' sounds like a description of the pig, but it is the definition, standing apart from the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Sallow skin has an unhealthy yellowish colour.

entries.clue: Street mass with song and prayer (3,5)

blocks.note: Ave. is short for avenue, a street
m = mass in physics
an aria is a solo song in an opera

annotation.surface: A church service in the street with music and prayers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mass' is the physicist's M, not the church service the surface suggests.
annotation.definitionFit: The Ave Maria, or Hail Mary, is a Catholic prayer to the Virgin Mary.

entries.clue: Limited number? (5,11)

blocks.note: the surface wants a restricted quantity; the setter means confined to one small area
the surface wants a figure; the setter means numb-er, a thing that numbs

annotation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a count, but here it is numb-er, a thing that numbs; 'limited' is a local effect.
annotation.definitionFit: A local anaesthetic numbs only a small part of the body.

entries.clue: It’s scary in empty wasteland; it’s sad when people go to work (7)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' puts EEK inside the letters of the emptied wasteland
indicatorNotes.empty: an emptied word has lost its contents, leaving only its outer letters W and D

blocks.note: 'eek!' is the cry of someone frightened
outer letters of wasteland
'ay' is an old cry of sorrow, as in 'ay me'

annotation.surface: A gloomy aside about an eerie waste ground and the Monday-morning commute.
annotation.walkthrough: Both 'it's' phrases stand for exclamations: EEK is what you say when scared, AY what you sigh when sad.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a weekday is a working day, Monday to Friday.

entries.clue: Peter wrestling with shark: monster morality tale (3,5,8)

indicatorNotes.wrestling: wrestlers twist and tangle together, so the letters of PETER and SHARK are rearranged

blocks.note: PETER and SHARK rearranged together
an ogress is a female ogre, a monster

annotation.surface: A boy's-adventure fable: Peter grapples with a shark and a monster.
annotation.walkthrough: The Rake's Progress is Hogarth's series of paintings showing a young heir's slide into ruin, later a Stravinsky opera.
annotation.definitionFit: Hogarth's picture series traces a wastrel's downfall as a moral warning, so it is a morality tale.

entries.clue: Retrieve key in Parisian street (6)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' is used literally: the key is placed inside the street, so ESC sits within RUE

blocks.note: Esc is the escape key on a keyboard
rue is French for street

annotation.surface: Going back for keys dropped in a Paris street.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Key' is the computer key Esc, not the door key the surface suggests.
annotation.definitionFit: To rescue something is to save or recover it, to retrieve it.

entries.clue: Sinister Six filling food stores with heroin (8)

indicatorNotes.filling: a filling goes inside something, so VI goes inside DELIS

blocks.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
delis are delicatessens, food shops
H is slang for heroin

annotation.surface: A gang of villains stocking food shops with drugs.
annotation.walkthrough: The Sinister Six are Spider-Man's villains, but 'Sinister' is the definition and 'Six' is just VI.
annotation.definitionFit: Devilish and sinister both mean wicked or threatening.

entries.clue: Another helping with no end of advice after sailor goes Awol (8)

indicatorNotes.with no: 'with no' removes the named letter from SECONDS
indicatorNotes.after: 'after' puts the shortened SECONDS behind AB

blocks.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
seconds are a second helping of food
last letter of advice, removed from SECONDS

annotation.surface: A sailor takes a second plate and then, ignoring advice, deserts.
annotation.walkthrough: Awol means absent without leave, military slang for deserting.
annotation.definitionFit: To go Awol is to leave without permission, which is to abscond.

entries.clue: Portuguese song of love following short-lived trend (4)

blocks.note: a fad is a brief craze
love is zero in tennis, O

annotation.surface: A love song that caught on and quickly faded.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Portuguese song of love' reads as one definition, but 'of love' is wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Fado is a mournful Portuguese folk song style.

entries.clue: Stared at as I cried audibly (9)

indicatorNotes.audibly: audibly means as heard, so the sound of the phrase counts, not its spelling

blocks.note: to bawl is to cry loudly

annotation.surface: Someone who wept and found people gawping at them.
annotation.walkthrough: Say 'I bawled' aloud and it runs together into the answer; 'as' just joins definition to wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: To eyeball someone is to stare at them hard.

entries.clue: Pivot finally bent, racing endlessly round circuit (8)

indicatorNotes.finally: finally picks out the last letter of 'bent'
indicatorNotes.endlessly: endlessly cuts the last letter off RUNNING
indicatorNotes.round: 'round' wraps the shortened word around O

blocks.note: last letter of bent
RUNNING without its last letter
a circuit is a loop, O

annotation.surface: A report of a buckled part on a racing car doing endless laps.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pivot' is the definition, not the source of the first letter; T comes from 'bent'.
annotation.definitionFit: A trunnion is a pin or pivot, like those on which a cannon barrel tilts.

entries.clue: Composer absorbing time with empty grandiosity and lack of energy (8)

indicatorNotes.absorbing: what is absorbed is taken in, so T goes inside LEHAR
indicatorNotes.empty: an emptied word keeps only its outer letters, G and Y

blocks.note: Franz Lehár wrote The Merry Widow
T = time
first and last letters of grandiosity

annotation.surface: A composer whose grand works take ages and leave everyone drained.
annotation.walkthrough: Elgar looks tempting with its E, L, G, A, R, but only Lehár leaves room for T and GY in the right order.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word names a state of drowsy sluggishness.

entries.clue: Gallery getting cold for end of waltz, enclosed in walls of sanctuary — it will do (11)

indicatorNotes.getting: UFFIZI gets C in place of a letter
indicatorNotes.for: 'for' means instead of, so C replaces Z
indicatorNotes.enclosed in: the pieces are placed inside the walls of sanctuary
indicatorNotes.walls of: the walls of a word are its first and last letters, S and Y

blocks.note: the Uffizi is the great art gallery in Florence
C = cold, as on a tap
last letter of waltz, swapped out for C
enc. is the abbreviation for enclosed, as at the foot of a letter
first and last letters of sanctuary

annotation.surface: A gallery's cold room hosting a waltz, tucked away in a sanctuary.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Enclosed' works twice: it gives ENC and, with 'in', puts the pieces inside S…Y.
annotation.definitionFit: A sufficiency is an adequate amount, something that will do.

entries.clue: Starchy stuff from unknown player of small part in valley (8)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' puts Y and COG inside GLEN

blocks.note: algebra's unknowns are x, y and z
a cog in the machine plays a small part in something big
a glen is a narrow valley, especially in Scotland

annotation.surface: An unknown bit-part actor digging up something starchy in a valley.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Player of small part' reads as a bit-part actor, but a cog is the small part in a machine.
annotation.definitionFit: Glycogen is the starch-like carbohydrate animals store in the liver and muscles.

entries.clue: Solemnly, teacher dashed around old early learning centre (10,6)

indicatorNotes.dashed: dashed means smashed or thrown about, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.around: 'around' brings O in with the rearranged letters

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters
O = old

annotation.surface: A grave teacher hurrying round an old nursery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dashed' looks like hurried, but it is the instruction to scramble.
annotation.definitionFit: An elementary school gives children their first years of education.

entries.clue: Problem with speech delivered back in Fresno? It all aligns (9)

indicatorNotes.back: 'back' means the letters are read right to left
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' says the answer sits inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run from the second L of 'aligns' back to the N of 'Fresno'

annotation.surface: A tourist's remark that everything lines up neatly in the Californian city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Delivered' belongs with the definition as a speech problem in delivery; the hidden letters read right to left across the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: Lallation is a speech defect in which L is said for R, or babyish speech.

entries.clue: Spooner’s delivery service takes in snack (5,3)

indicatorNotes.Spooner’s: Rev. Spooner swapped the first sounds of words, so the opening sounds are exchanged

blocks.note: the mail is a delivery service; its opening M sound is swapped for TR
to trick someone is to take them in; its opening TR sound is swapped for M

annotation.surface: A courier company caught stealing snacks from the parcels.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Takes in' looks like a container instruction, but it means deceives: TRICKS.
annotation.definitionFit: Trail mix is a snack of nuts and dried fruit carried by hikers.

entries.clue: I don’t care about principal character in Social Network (4)

indicatorNotes.about: MEH goes about, around, the letter
indicatorNotes.principal character in: the principal character of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: 'meh' is a shrug of indifference
first letter of Social

annotation.surface: A shrug at the lead actor of the film The Social Network.
annotation.walkthrough: The Social Network is a film title, which hides that 'Network' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A mesh is a net or network of interlaced strands.

entries.clue: Historical Russian museum losing millions (8)

indicatorNotes.losing: a museum losing millions has them taken away, so the M is removed

blocks.note: the Hermitage is the great art museum in St Petersburg
M = millions, removed

annotation.surface: A famous Russian museum hit by a funding cut.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Historical' is an adjective, so the answer must work as one too: a heritage site is a historical one.
annotation.definitionFit: Heritage used as an adjective, as in a heritage railway, means historical.

entries.clue: Earth is first-class in Georgia (4)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' is used literally: first-class is placed in Georgia, so AI sits within GA

blocks.note: A1 means first-class, written with I for the 1
GA is the postal code for Georgia

annotation.surface: A proud Georgian's claim that the soil back home is the best.
annotation.walkthrough: A1 appears as AI because crosswords treat the figure 1 as the letter I.
annotation.definitionFit: Gaia is the Greek personification of the Earth, and a name for the planet as a living whole.

entries.clue: Agreement is embodied in current digital format (7,4)

indicatorNotes.embodied in: what is embodied in something is held within it, so IS goes inside DC

blocks.note: a compact is a formal agreement
the word itself
DC is direct current

annotation.surface: A deal that is written into the latest streaming format.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'up to date', which suits a digital format, but it is electrical current here.
annotation.definitionFit: The compact disc was the first mass-market digital audio format.

entries.clue: Spots top pilot around end of afternoon (4)

indicatorNotes.end of: the end of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: an ace is a star fighter pilot
last letter of afternoon

annotation.surface: Someone sighting a top gun flying overhead in the late afternoon.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spots' looks like a verb, sees, but it is the noun: pimples.
annotation.definitionFit: Acne is a skin condition that causes spots.

entries.clue: Celebration following old PM’s powerful blow (11)

blocks.note: Lord North was British prime minister 1770-82
Easter is a Christian festival

annotation.surface: A party thrown after a former prime minister's knockout punch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blow' reads as a punch, but it is a gale; the 's after PM is just the join.
annotation.definitionFit: A northeaster is a strong wind from the northeast.

entries.clue: Enjoy books about the old British loaf (3,5)

indicatorNotes.about: READ goes about, around, YE and BR

blocks.note: to enjoy books is to read
ye is the old spelling of 'the', as in Ye Olde Shoppe
Br. = British

annotation.surface: An old Briton who likes reading and baking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The old' is a crossword staple for YE, from signs like Ye Olde Tea Shoppe.
annotation.definitionFit: Rye bread is baked as loaves, so a loaf defines it by type.

entries.clue: Cocktail shaken containing dash of Drambuie (3,3,5)

indicatorNotes.shaken: a shaken cocktail is mixed up, so the letters of 'containing' plus D are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters
first letter of Drambuie

annotation.surface: A bartender's recipe: a drink shaken with a splash of whisky liqueur.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Containing' looks like an instruction to put something inside, but it is the fodder itself.
annotation.definitionFit: Loosely, a gin and tonic is a mixed drink, so a cocktail.

entries.clue: Metalworker isn’t playing with German hydrogen (8)

indicatorNotes.playing: letters that are playing are moving about, so ISNT is rearranged

blocks.note: ISNT rearranged
mit is German for with
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

annotation.surface: A metalworker declining to experiment with German hydrogen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With German' is one unit: the German word for 'with', MIT.
annotation.definitionFit: A tinsmith works in tin and other light metal.

entries.clue: Reluctant to follow revolutionary with ultimately sterile, dry material (11)

indicatorNotes.to follow: LOTH comes to follow the other pieces, at the end
indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately picks out the last letter of 'sterile'

blocks.note: Che Guevara, the Marxist revolutionary
last letter of sterile
sec is French for dry, used of wine
loth is a spelling of loath, reluctant

annotation.surface: A reluctant rebel following a sterile, dry routine.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue opens with LOTH but it goes last; 'to follow' sends it behind the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: Cheesecloth is a loosely woven cotton material.

entries.clue: Tricky situation before detective arrived with books (11)

blocks.note: pre- means before
a DI is a detective inspector
came = arrived
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

annotation.surface: Trouble brewing before a detective turns up carrying files.
annotation.walkthrough: NT for 'books' is the New Testament, a crossword convention, along with OT for the Old.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word names a fix or jam that is hard to get out of.

entries.clue: Little drink after film, a form of therapy (11)

blocks.note: Psycho is Hitchcock's 1960 thriller
a dram is a small measure of spirits
the word itself

annotation.surface: A nightcap after a thriller, as a kind of self-medication.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A form of therapy' looks like a whole definition, but the 'a' is the last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Psychodrama is a therapy in which patients act out their problems.

entries.clue: Hostile, like Lil? (3-8)

blocks.note: unfriendly, badly inclined towards someone
the name LIL is made of the letters of a three-letter word for sick, laid out afresh

annotation.walkthrough: 'Disposed' here means arranged, so LIL is literally ILL laid out differently.
annotation.definitionFit: A double definition: the idiom for unfriendly feeling, and a joke reading where 'disposed' means laid out, so sick letters rearranged.

entries.clue: Local cows without water? (4)

blocks.note: 'local' flags a dialect word for cattle
how you order whisky with nothing added

annotation.surface: Cattle in a drought-stricken field.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Local' flags the dialect word: neat meaning cattle survives in rural speech and in 'neatsfoot oil'.
annotation.definitionFit: Neat is dialect for cattle, and neat whisky has no water added.

entries.clue: Society thief denied introduction in New York’s elitist attitude (8)

indicatorNotes.denied introduction: a word denied its introduction loses its first letter

blocks.note: S = society
a robber is a thief; drop the R
NY = New York

annotation.surface: A society burglar refused entry to a snooty New York party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Denied introduction' reads as being refused entry to a party, but it just drops the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Snobbery is the attitude of looking down on those of lower status.

entries.clue: Partner supporting graduate exactly as set out, in general terms (9)

indicatorNotes.supporting: in a down clue, a support sits underneath, so ALLY comes below

blocks.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts
sic marks a quotation copied exactly, errors included
an ally is a partner

annotation.surface: A spouse backing a new graduate, to put it simply.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Exactly as set out' describes sic, the Latin note printed after a quoted mistake.
annotation.definitionFit: Basically means fundamentally, speaking in general terms.

entries.clue: Give evidence on return of more sickly recidivism (9)

annotation.definitionNote: recidivism is a noun; relapsing is used here as the gerund, the act of falling back

indicatorNotes.return of: a return goes back the way it came, so PALER is read right to left

blocks.note: paler = more pallid, sicklier-looking
to sing is slang for informing to the police

annotation.surface: An informer testifying about a sickly repeat offender.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Give evidence' comes first in the clue but last in the answer; 'on' just joins.
annotation.definitionFit: Recidivism is falling back into crime, so relapsing into bad ways.

entries.clue: Hand over unopened bubbly without making much effort (9)

indicatorNotes.unopened: an unopened word has lost its first letter

blocks.note: to pass is to hand over
bubbly = lively; drop the L

annotation.surface: Handing over a bottle of champagne without bothering to open it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bubbly' suggests champagne, especially with 'unopened', but it means lively.
annotation.definitionFit: To act passively is to go along without taking an active part.

entries.clue: Tell about centre of language control (8)

indicatorNotes.about: RELATE goes about, around, the middle letters
indicatorNotes.centre of: the centre of an eight-letter word is its two middle letters

blocks.note: to relate a story is to tell it
middle two letters of lanGUage

annotation.surface: An account of the brain's language-control centre.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the brain's speech centre, but 'centre of language' is just GU.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean keeping something in check by rules or adjustment.

entries.clue: Key Xmas song arranged for air travellers’ backup (6,5)

indicatorNotes.arranged: an arranged piece of music is rewritten, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

annotation.surface: A Christmas carol arranged in a new key for an in-flight singalong.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Key' and 'arranged' feel musical, but both belong to the anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: oxygen masks drop down in a plane if cabin pressure fails.

entries.clue: Done with friend coming up to share some space (7)

indicatorNotes.coming up: in a down clue, coming up means read bottom to top, so PAL becomes LAP

blocks.note: over = finished, done
a pal is a friend

annotation.surface: Finished with a mate who comes up to bunk down in your room.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Done' is OVER as in 'the game is over', not a verb of action.
annotation.definitionFit: Two things overlap when they partly occupy the same space.

entries.clue: Sign with fashionable cladding is least original (8)

indicatorNotes.cladding: cladding covers the outside of something, so HOT goes around ARIES

blocks.note: Aries is a sign of the zodiac
hot = very fashionable

annotation.surface: A trendy horoscope is the most derivative of the lot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sign' is a star sign; the zodiac supplies ARIES, LEO and the rest to crossword setters.
annotation.definitionFit: Hoary means old and trite, so the hoariest joke is the least original.

entries.clue: Single daughter, say, flipping nervous (2,4)

indicatorNotes.flipping: to flip something is to turn it over, so EG is read backwards

blocks.note: single = one
D = daughter
e.g. = for example, say

annotation.surface: A single mother's daughter is flipping jittery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British swear-word intensifier, but it turns EG round.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a person on edge is keyed up, as if balanced at a brink.

entries.clue: Tool works steadily to overcome resistance (6)

indicatorNotes.to overcome: in a down clue, to overcome is to sit on top of and around, so PLIES wraps R

blocks.note: to ply a trade is to work at it steadily
R = resistance in physics

annotation.surface: A tool that keeps at it until the stubborn part gives way.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Works steadily' is one verb phrase, PLIES, as a ferry plies its route.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain hypernym: the answer is one kind of hand tool, used for gripping and bending.

entries.clue: Nice cat modelled around American ceramics technique (9)

indicatorNotes.modelled: clay that is modelled is reshaped, so the letters of NICE CAT are rearranged
indicatorNotes.around: the rearranged letters go around US

blocks.note: NICECAT rearranged
US = American

annotation.surface: A pleasant cat figurine, modelled around an American pottery method.
annotation.walkthrough: Nice may be the French city, but here it is just letters; 'modelled' suits the pottery surface.
annotation.definitionFit: Encaustic work fuses colour into tiles or pottery by burning it in.

entries.clue: Ending with ersatz answer (4)

blocks.note: ersatz means fake; the fish word used as an adjective, as in mock Latin, carries that sense
A = answer

annotation.surface: A plea for a conclusion with a phoney answer.
annotation.walkthrough: COD for 'ersatz' is the adjective meaning mock, not the fish.
annotation.definitionFit: A coda is the closing section of a piece of music.

entries.clue: Work with conventional scale, including one according to choice (8)

blocks.note: op. = opus, a musical work
tonal music uses the conventional major and minor scales
I is one in Roman numerals

annotation.surface: A composition in a traditional key, with one part left to the player.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Work' is the musical opus, abbreviated OP, which suits the scale in the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: Optional means left to your choice.

entries.clue: Tongue served up in Alice’s Restaurant (4)

indicatorNotes.served up in: 'up' in a down clue reads the letters bottom to top, and 'in' says they sit inside the phrase

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words: the end of Alice's and the start of Restaurant, read upwards

annotation.surface: Ox tongue on the menu at the diner in the Arlo Guthrie song.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' sounds like a dish in a restaurant, but it means a language.
annotation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic language of Scotland or Ireland.

entries.clue: A dupe sent back hot bathroom accessory (6)

indicatorNotes.sent back: what is sent back returns the way it came, so A FOOL is read right to left

blocks.note: a dupe is a fool
H = hot, as on a tap

annotation.surface: A gullible shopper returns a hot-water gadget for the bathroom.
annotation.walkthrough: Only A FOOL is sent back; H is added afterwards, unreversed.
annotation.definitionFit: A loofah is a dried plant sponge used for scrubbing in the bath.

entries.clue: Clear one pedestal abroad for antiquity relocated to London or NYC (10,6)

annotation.definition: antiquity relocated to London or NYC

indicatorNotes.abroad: abroad can mean all over the place, scattered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 16 letters

annotation.surface: Clearing a plinth overseas to ship an ancient monument to a new home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' fits the surface of shipping monuments overseas, but it is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Cleopatra's Needles are ancient Egyptian obelisks moved to London's Embankment and New York's Central Park.

entries.clue: Quietly change and prevaricate (6)

blocks.note: p = piano, quietly in music
to alter is to change

annotation.surface: Advice to shift your story quietly and dodge the question.
annotation.walkthrough: P for quietly comes from piano, the musical marking for soft.
annotation.definitionFit: To palter is to talk evasively or deal insincerely, to prevaricate.

entries.clue: Leaders of youth can’t hack walk, it said, after 50: stop just short of final destination (8)

annotation.definition: stop just short of final destination

indicatorNotes.Leaders of: leaders are the front letters of each word
indicatorNotes.it said: 'it said' means the word as spoken, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: L is 50 in Roman numerals
first letters of youth, can't, hack
a gait is a way of walking

annotation.surface: Young people who can't manage the walk, tired out past fifty metres before the finish.
annotation.walkthrough: A lychgate is the roofed gateway to a churchyard, where a coffin once rested before burial, so it is the last stop before the grave.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the coffin paused at the lychgate just before reaching its grave.

entries.clue: Problem with skin or hair that could leave monster stranded? (7)

blocks.note: dry skin and dry hair are common complaints
split the word in two: a lake that has gone dry would beach its famous Scottish monster

annotation.walkthrough: The monster is the Loch Ness monster of Scottish legend; split the answer as DRY NESS to see the joke.
annotation.definitionFit: A double definition: a complaint of skin and hair lacking moisture, and whimsically a state of Loch Ness drained dry.
